title: Secure SDK flows: API key rotation, SSO token lifetimes, and ergonomic patterns
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers and platform teams repeatedly ask for clearer guidance and built-in helpers for secure API key rotation, SSO token handling for enterprise orgs, and concrete examples across Python/TypeScript/Go. Current SDKs have fragmented patterns: some expose low-level token objects, others hide refresh entirely, and none include a recommended rotation rollout workflow or examples for ephemeral credentials (short-lived API keys backed by KMS/HSM).
objective: Deliver a cross-language set of SDK primitives and docs that: (1) make rotating keys straightforward for customers without breaking in-flight requests, (2) provide a standardized SSO token refresh/validation pattern for enterprise flows, (3) offer prescriptive secret-handling guidance (env vars, file perms, CI secrets), and (4) ship example migration guides and sample apps in Python/TS/Go.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) expose a single opinionated helper for injecting credentials that supports hot-swap rotation without restarting the process
Documentation includes a step-by-step key rotation playbook and an enterprise SSO token lifecycle example (OIDC refresh and short-lived session tokens)
E2E tests covering: rotating a key while concurrent streaming/generation requests are in-flight; token refresh failure and graceful fallback; and automated CI secret rotation integration
Security review sign-off recorded in the ticket and confluence doc
Migration example repos (one per language) added to /examples/sdk-key-rotation with readme and scripts
notes: Technical approach: introduce CredentialProvider interface (language-specific name) that supports get(), refresh(), and on_rotate(callback). SDK internals will call get() for token fetch and subscribe to on_rotate to atomically swap live credentials for new ones.
Rotation model: recommend short-lived signing keys (T=1h) with automated server-side rotation + stable verification keychain. Provide example of issuing ephemeral API key via KMS-signed JWT exchange.
SSO guidance: document OIDC refresh best practices, recommended clamp on refresh attempts (exponential backoff), and how to escalate to interactive reauth in CLI apps.

Secret handling: enforce / recommend env var names (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_SSO_TOKEN), avoid storing long-lived secrets in repo, recommend secrets manager integrations (AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, HashiCorp Vault) with code snippets.

Streaming ergonomics: ensure in-flight streaming requests continue using previous credential until a safe boundary (end-of-stream or token expiry threshold) then switch. Provide cancellation semantics for forced immediate rotate.
Backward compatibility: provide adapter shims for existing SDK users; deprecation plan documented in CHANGELOG and migration guide.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge provider interfaces into beta branch; add feature flags for rotation helpers
Week 2: Land language idiomatic implementations and minimal examples; run E2E on staging cluster
Week 3: Internal dogfood — enable auto-rotation for a small set of internal customers and monitor metrics
Week 4: Publish docs, example repos, and SDK minor releases; announce breaking changes/migration path
Post-release: 2-week observability window and iterate on edge cases reported by customers
monitoring_requirements: New telemetry: rotation_success, rotation_failure, rotation_latency (ms), active_credential_version
SLOs: rotation success >= 99.9% within configured window
Alert: >1% rotation failures across requests for 10m triggers P1 ops runbook
risky_decisions: Atomic swap semantics for streaming: chosen approach keeps old token valid for in-flight streams. Risk: longer-lived token exposure for a short window versus risk of breaking in-progress calls.
Auto-rotate default: enabled for Dedicated/Private customers on new SDKs; default off for hosted in case customers rely on sticky long-lived keys. This divergence needs clear docs to avoid confusion.
